# Complete v4 variable-transform adoption

The active combined goal covers #455 and #463. Its integration baseline is v4 main `b157988355d2fabb6cbc62d56de18b203456897f`, which merged PR #464. MATLAB APIs, saved scientific records, canonical coefficient ordering and numerical tolerances remain unchanged. The separate v5 checkout is outside this work.

## Implementation sequence

1. Bound duplicate full-grid derivative preparation for pruned execution (#463). Preserve every resolved Fourier frequency, even-grid Nyquist derivative rules, scalar operations and event-owned fields. Compare with the existing pruned candidate as well as the frozen production schedule.
2. Adapt the frozen benchmark `compact-general-fused-views-v1` implementation to actual WVM coefficient construction and output projection. Integrate shared-matrix Stratified QG/Hydrostatic first, then exact-group Boussinesq. Retain the optimized interleaved path as the bounded control. Preserve phase, mean/inertial modes, cross-family projection, vertical velocity and displacement/stratification terms.
3. Wire the qualified execution/backend policy through native runtime and supported MATLAB-loaded paths. Apply final benchmark #23 topology defaults, with bounded pointwise calibration and no process-wide BLAS environment mutation.
4. Qualify independent source builds and representative full workloads, adopt passing defaults, merge reviewable increments and update issue acceptance records. A candidate failing its declared gate remains rejected or deferred with evidence; passing correctness alone does not establish adoption.

The benchmark source is pinned at `6f2e4cd9e2f092433a584645e573d818ecaca42b`. Its committed handoff and final decisions supersede historical primitive sweeps. No repeated DGEMM/ZGEMM packing survey, small-grid timing/crossover work, zero-fill survey, speculative custom arithmetic, or v5 optimization belongs to this goal. New algorithm research requires a demonstrated material residual bottleneck in actual integrated execution.

## Qualification boundaries

Each campaign must freeze its sources, binaries, fixture hashes, workload definitions, effective topology, trial counts and gates before timing. The existing #464 receipts remain historical screening evidence. Reused scientific fixtures retain their original generator/source identities; their outputs must never be relabeled as newly generated.

The principal performance sizes remain 256×256×129 and 512×512×257 where applicable. Small, odd and nonsquare fixtures establish correctness only. Complete native flux, MATLAB-loaded execution where supported, and matched model integration are separate boundaries. Scalar, particle, event/diagnostic and output work must be included rather than inferred from flux-only timings. Exact grouped Boussinesq requires an explicit capacity estimate before generating large fixtures.

Final variable adoption requires at least 10% geometric complete-flux improvement, no declared large profile slower than 1.03× control, paired uncertainty excluding a tie, no peak-memory growth, unchanged scientific checks and prepared execution with no application allocation, plan construction or worker creation. Report preparation, numerical execution, adapters, output, owned capacities, provider lower bounds and fresh-process peak RSS separately. Record rejection and failed runs along with successful evidence.

## Prospective derivative-resource screen (#463)

Before new large timing, compare three independently identified selections: the frozen full-FFT production path at `b1579883`, the prior pruned/streamed path at the same revision, and the bounded-derivative pruned/streamed candidate. Compile the same author-only workers against the two source trees; record both source trees and the separate harness identity. The frozen checkout is `wvm-v4-issue455-variable-control`.

Use the existing independently generated SQG/Hydrostatic fixtures at 256×256×129 and 512×512×257, preserving their original `55dd8ae` provenance and hashes. Compare flux payloads with the stored MATLAB oracle. Add a manufactured horizontal scalar-advection workload containing low frequencies, resolved frequencies outside retained truncation and even-grid Nyquist terms, with depth-dependent amplitudes and supplied constant horizontal velocity. Compare with its independent analytical derivative and the frozen source output. This scalar workload isolates full-grid derivative resources; it does not qualify three-dimensional scalar integration, filtering or event behavior by itself.

For each family/grid/workload run four fresh-process blocks, alternating the three selections in forward/reverse block order, two warmups and four measured calls. FFTW internal workers stay one; pruned horizontal workers stay twelve; matrix backend is Accelerate with the existing process BLAS settings recorded. Run a one-block, no-warmup, one-sample smoke first; it has no timing acceptance role. Keep all reports and sample journals. Retain the first payload per selection/profile plus every failure, and hash then remove only later successful duplicate outputs after comparisons pass. This retention policy bounds new disk use without discarding existing campaign evidence.

Report candidate/prior-pruned and candidate/production time ratios and peak RSS separately. #463 requires no greater than 3% slowdown on declared large representative work and no peak-memory growth; these direct scalar/flux screens inform that decision but do not replace the parent event, independent MATLAB and full-model gates. Freeze the candidate source and build identities before the large screen; retain any failed screen instead of changing its limits after measurement.

## Compact integration and capacity preflight

The compact candidate now passes direct representation views through actual coefficient assembly, horizontal transforms and shared/exact-group vertical operators. It retains canonical interleaved coefficients at public boundaries. Exact groups are split only into maximal contiguous runs in their existing order; group identities, matrix values and matrix membership remain authoritative. Boussinesq nonlinear execution uses six real volumes and preserves all four target spectra for final wave/balanced projection. Runtime construction accepts an explicit matrix-backend/execution service; its default remains the scalar, established schedule until qualification.

Focused verification before pointwise-worker integration: SQG and Hydrostatic MATLAB comparisons passed all five methods across nine provider/schedule configurations; Boussinesq passed all five methods, including discontiguous groups and nonuniform vertical grids. Hydrostatic and Boussinesq kernel tests passed with ASan/UBSan; exact-group vertical operator checks passed Release and ASan/UBSan. The three runtime service-injection tests passed. These checks also exposed and corrected SQG setup's premature destruction of an existing engine on failed creation.

MATLAB capacity preflight reused the saved 256/512 SQG horizontal wavenumbers and exactly evaluated the Boussinesq `unique(sqrt(k.*k+l.*l).^2)` expression. The 256×256×129 grid has Nj=85 and 3,374 groups: its four wave projection/reconstruction arrays, cross-family array and three group vectors require about 1.291 GiB. The 512×512×257 grid has Nj=170 and 13,336 groups: the same arrays require about 20.287 GiB before C++ prepared copies, model state or outputs. Available disk at preflight was about 15.88 GiB. Generate the full 256 fixture; exclude the 512 Boussinesq fixture on this host, preserving its declared shape rather than reducing modes or changing exact grouping. This exclusion is a qualification limitation, not a passing large-profile result.

The next direct-flux campaign compares independently built baseline production/pruned selections with candidate interleaved/compact selections. Candidate representation, actual backend identifier and effective pointwise worker count must be observed. Builds require receipts tying source hashes and commit to worker hashes and the separately identified harness; historical control harness provenance remains explicit. Four process blocks form a pilot; eight form final qualification; each has two warmups and four measured calls. Alternate selection order by block. Retain first successful payloads per profile/selection and every failure; hash then remove only later successfully compared duplicates. Complete child-process RSS comes from `wait4` after exit. A direct-flux result alone cannot close the complete-model adoption gates.

## Final campaign freeze

The independent baseline is `b157988355d2fabb6cbc62d56de18b203456897f`; the compact candidate is `a3acbf4dc9305c4d656399e9f98bc8360ddfa66f`. Clean MATLAB path qualification passed all ten transform methods, and a clean-path read-only oracle recheck reproduced all five large saved flux payloads bitwise. The 45-run bounded calibration of the benchmark finalists' pointwise counts (1, 4, 8) selected eight workers across the five large profiles. Together with the twelve-run direct smoke and eight-run complete-model smoke, this supplies the pilot readiness evidence; proceed directly to the independent eight-block final campaign without repeating a separate four-block pilot. Calibration samples are excluded from final acceptance statistics.

Final direct profiles are SQG and Hydrostatic at both declared sizes and exact-group Boussinesq at 256×256×129. Each final process has two warmup calls and four measured calls; use its median as the paired process observation. Compare compact with production, prior-pruned and candidate interleaved, retaining every comparison. Use equal profile weighting of mean log paired ratios and 10,000 within-profile paired bootstrap resamples (seed 455) for the aggregate 95% interval. Apply the previously declared 0.90 geometric flux, 1.03 maximum profile ratio and interval-excludes-tie gates against production. Also report the 1.03 prior-pruned regression gate required by #463. Owned capacities must not grow; report per-profile peak RSS ratios and require no per-profile geometric RSS growth. Timing or memory failures remain failures and cannot be discarded by selecting a subset after measurement.

The complete-model final campaigns use SQG, Hydrostatic and Boussinesq at 256×256×129, one fixed RK4 step (four RHS evaluations), a full-volume tracer, coefficient output and off-step dense velocity output; Hydrostatic and Boussinesq also advance particles. Two warmup process blocks precede eight measured blocks, rotating the four selections. Validate the complete saved NetCDF graphs against independently integrated MATLAB records and the frozen model. Require no profile integration slowdown beyond 1.03 and no growth in owned retained memory or geometric complete-process RSS. Report preparation, integration, close/output and total lifetime separately. The representative model profiles complement the larger direct-flux profiles; they do not qualify 512 model workloads. Preserve that exclusion in the final adoption decision and follow-up scope.

Before model timing, capacity review established that Boussinesq 256 is feasible and should be included, superseding its provisional scope exclusion. Its separate fixture restores the existing exact saved modal record rather than recalculating eigenmodes, preserving its initial time and advancing one half-second step. Keep first successful model outputs per selection and every failure. Compare later successful outputs against the independent MATLAB graph and retained control, hash them and remove them incrementally to bound the live disk working set. After an entire profile finishes, first outputs may be losslessly compressed, with decompressed SHA256 verification before deleting the uncompressed copy; archive work occurs between timing campaigns. This preserves the complete first payloads while leaving room for subsequent profiles.
